newsitem.title: CHINA: China insurance sector cautious on opening up.
newsitem.headline: China insurance sector cautious on opening up.

text.p: China's insurance industry should be cautious in opening its doors to foreign competitors to avoid being overwhelmed by experienced foreign firms, the Financial News said on Tuesday.
While foreign companies could offer valuable experience and training to domestic firms, opening China's insurance market too quickly would only harm Chinese insurers, the newspaper said.
China's state-owned insurance firms were fettered by a 55 percent income tax and a 15 percent regulatory tax while foreign firms were taxed just 15 percent, the commentary said.
Foreign insurers were also free of state restrictions on domestic companies that prevented them from freely reinvesting their earnings, it said.
"Setting free the whole insurance market under these conditions would undoubtedly drown China's insurance industry" it said.
"China's insurance circles naturally will not lightly hand over such a vast market," it said.
Other official media said last week China's central bank was drafting regulations under which the number of foreign insurance companies operating in China could be increased.
A Hong Kong unit of Manufacturers Life Insurance Co of Canada is setting up China's first life insurance joint venture, Zhang Hong Life Insurance Co.
American International Assurance Co Ltd of the United States and Japan's Tokio Marine and Fire Insurance Co Ltd are the only two foreign insurance firms currently allowed to issue policies in China.
Many other foreign insurance companies have set up representative offices in China.
